title: Assumption registry — v1.0
description: Chainlink #59, plan.md §8.4. A governed registry of assumptions, each with a STABLE assumption_id, the canonical assumption TEXT (not just a hash), a content hash RECOMPUTED from that stored text by scripts/assumption_registry.py:canonical_assumption_hash(), a tracking_issue, and provenance/history. This supersedes neither docs/boundary-contract-schema.json's composite assumption_ref nor the cross-boundary collision detector — those remain valid (phase A) and are dual-resolved with registry IDs (phase B); the composite form is only removed in a declared breaking version (phase D), which this schema's own schema_version participates in. Registry documents live under a workspace's specs/_assumptions/*.json.

schema_version.description: The reference-resolution era this registry declares. Major 1.x = dual-resolution (registry ID or legacy composite both resolve). A future 2.0 declares legacy composite support removed (phase D); scripts/assumption_registry.py refuses an unknown major rather than reinterpreting it.

entries.description: One entry per canonical assumption. Two entries sharing an assumption_id anywhere in a workspace make every reference to that id ambiguous, which the registry gate reports as a hard error.

assumption_id.description: The stable identity, chosen once and never recycled. Survives boundary/method renames and canonical-text edits, unlike the composite (boundary_id, tracking_issue, assumption_hash) which changes whenever any component does.

canonical_text.description: The assumption's actual normative content. A reference resolving to an id resolves to THIS text; the hash is derived from it, never the reverse.

content_hash.description: RECOMPUTED from canonical_text by scripts/assumption_registry.py:canonical_assumption_hash(). Unlike docs/boundary-contract-schema.json's bare declared assumption_hash, the gate recomputes this at load time and fails on disagreement, so it is a real content binding, not a typed string.

tracking_issue.description: Where the acceptance/risk decision for this assumption is tracked, e.g. chainlink:713.

boundary_ids.description: Optional declared homes for this assumption. Informational: the gate's composite-ref resolution matches on (tracking_issue, assumption_hash), not on this list, so a boundary rename does not by itself break a reference once the id is used.

provenance.description: Append-only history, oldest first: who added or changed the canonical text and when. A canonical_text edit without a matching provenance append (and a re-signed content_hash) is reported as hash-disagreeing, not silently accepted.
